en.heading: 22–25 February: four days of EDSA People Power remembrance
en.origin: EDSA People Power Commemoration Week remembers the four days of demonstrations from 22 to 25 February 1986, when a broad non-violent public movement ended the authoritarian rule of Ferdinand Marcos and renewed Philippine democratic institutions. Executive Order No. 82 of 22 February 1999 created the EDSA People Power Commission to preserve and explain the legacy of that revolution. The government's commission was established years after the original 1986 events. Presidential Proclamation No. 1224, signed 30 January 2007, specifically designated 22–25 February of each year as the commemorative week and asked authorities, civil organizations and the public to participate. Its name 'week' does not turn four days into a seven-day period or make them automatically non-working.

en.purpose: Remember the 1986 non-violent democratic movement while accurately reporting the four-day anniversary and later legal chronology.

en.heading: Third Sunday of January: the Philippines' day for the protection of human life
en.origin: The Day of Sanctity and Protection of Human Life is a Philippine civic observance framed around respect for life and family. Its presidential text uses a religiously informed moral argument and references constitutional language about protection of mothers and unborn life. Proclamation No. 490, signed by President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo on 22 October 2003, officially designated the third Sunday of January of every year, rather than a fixed numbered date or a whole month. The proclamation cites Article II, sections 5 and 12 of the Philippine Constitution. It is not the same legal observance as an independent Children's Day entry on the same Sunday unless a separate, verifiable instrument is found, and it does not make that Sunday a regular national non-working holiday.

Il provvedimento richiama l'articolo II, sezioni 5 e 12 della Costituzione. en.heading: 18–24 October: how United Nations Week became annual in the Philippines
en.origin: United Nations Week in the Philippines recalls the United Nations' establishment in 1945 and invites discussion of international peace, human dignity, cooperation, development and the Philippines' participation as an original UN member. Proclamation No. 276 of 16 October 2002 declared 18–24 October 2002 a one-year Philippine United Nations Week, highlighting international themes including mountains, ecotourism and cultural heritage. Proclamation No. 483, signed 6 October 2003, explicitly repeated the period 18–24 October and added 'every year thereafter', appointing the Department of Foreign Affairs to lead. United Nations Day on 24 October is related but not identical to a seven-day Philippine week.

it.heading: 18–24 ottobre: quando la Settimana ONU divenne annuale nelle Filippine
it.origin: La Settimana delle Nazioni Unite nelle Filippine ricorda la nascita dell'ONU nel 1945 e invita a riflettere su pace, dignità umana, cooperazione, sviluppo e partecipazione del paese come membro fondatore. La Proclamazione n. 276 del 16 ottobre 2002 stabilì il 18–24 ottobre 2002 per la settimana ONU, con temi legati a montagne, ecoturismo e patrimonio culturale, riferiti a quell'anno. La Proclamazione n. 483 del 6 ottobre 2003 ribadì il 18–24 ottobre e aggiunse 'ogni anno successivo', affidando il coordinamento agli Affari esteri. Il 24 ottobre è la giornata ONU, non la stessa cosa della settimana nazionale.

Oktober 2003 führte den 18. bis 24. Oktober 'in jedem folgenden Jahr' ein und beauftragte das Außenministerium. Der UN-Tag am 24. ist vom nationalen Wochenzeitraum zu unterscheiden.
de.promoter: Department of Foreign Affairs and Philippine UN offices with government, local and civic organizations sind die in philippinischen Präsidialerlassen zur Durchführung oder Unterstützung genannten Einrichtungen.
de.purpose: UN-Prinzipien fördern und die einmalige Woche 2002 von der jährlichen Regelung 2003 trennen.
facts: Die UN-Woche auf den Philippinen erinnert an die Gründung der Vereinten Nationen 1945 und regt Gespräche über Frieden, Menschenwürde, Zusammenarbeit und philippinische Mitgliedschaft an.
Proklamation Nr. 276 vom 16. Oktober 2002 legte den 18. bis 24. Oktober nur für 2002 fest und behandelte Berge, Ökotourismus und Kulturerbe.

Proklamation Nr. 483 vom 6. Oktober 2003 führte den 18. bis 24. Oktober 'in jedem folgenden Jahr' ein und beauftragte das Außenministerium. Der UN-Tag am 24. ist vom nationalen Wochenzeitraum zu unterscheiden.

pt.heading: 18–24 de outubro: a Semana das Nações Unidas nas Filipinas
pt.origin: A Semana das Nações Unidas nas Filipinas recorda a criação da ONU em 1945 e promove reflexão sobre paz, dignidade, cooperação, desenvolvimento e participação filipina como membro fundador. A Proclamação n.º 276 de 16 de outubro de 2002 estabeleceu 18 a 24 de outubro de 2002, com temas de montanhas, ecoturismo e património cultural. A Proclamação n.º 483 de 6 de outubro de 2003 fixou 18 a 24 de outubro 'em todos os anos seguintes', com coordenação dos Negócios Estrangeiros. O Dia da ONU de 24 de outubro é distinto da semana.
pt.promoter: Department of Foreign Affairs and Philippine UN offices with government, local and civic organizations são as instituições chamadas pelas proclamações presidenciais filipinas a coordenar esta comemoração.
pt.purpose: Promover princípios da ONU distinguindo a semana única de 2002 da regra anual de 2003.

A Proclamação n.º 276 de 16 de outubro de 2002 estabeleceu 18 a 24 de outubro de 2002, com temas de montanhas, ecoturismo e património cultural.
A Proclamação n.º 483 de 6 de outubro de 2003 fixou 18 a 24 de outubro 'em todos os anos seguintes', com coordenação dos Negócios Estrangeiros. O Dia da ONU de 24 de outubro é distinto da semana.
